desc:
You compress a lowercase string s by cutting it into consecutive pieces and writing every piece in one of two ways:

  • a single letter is written as it is, and costs 1;
  • a piece that consists of a non-empty block u repeated r ≥ 2 times is written as the decimal number r followed by the block u, and costs digits(r) + |u|.

The pieces are written one after another and the cost of the encoding is the sum of the costs. Return the minimum possible cost.

s = "aaaaaaaaaaaa"    (12 times a)   result = 3    ("12a")
s = "abababab"                       result = 3    ("4ab")
s = "abcabcabcxyz"                   result = 7    ("3abc" + "x" + "y" + "z")
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: Let dp[i] be the best cost for the first i letters. A new piece ends at i: it is either one letter or a repeated block.
For a fixed start j, which substrings s[j:j+L] are a block repeated at least twice? A substring of length L is a repetition of its shortest period d exactly when d divides L (and then r = L / d).

Compute the prefix function (KMP failure array) of s[j:] for each start j. For every length L, the shortest period is d = L - pi[L-1]; if d divides L and L/d ≥ 2, relax dp[j+L] with dp[j] + digits(L/d) + d.
editorial: This is a shortest-path / DP over positions: dp[i] is the minimum cost for the prefix of length i, with dp[0] = 0. From a state dp[j] there is the single-letter transition to j+1 with cost 1, and one transition to j+L for every L such that s[j:j+L] is a block repeated at least twice. There is no need to try blocks that are not the shortest period: a longer block u repeated fewer times saves at most as many digits as it adds letters, so it is never strictly cheaper.

The shortest period of every prefix of s[j:] comes from one run of the KMP prefix function: the prefix of length L has period d = L - pi[L-1], and it is an exact repetition when d divides L. Doing this for every start j costs O(n) each, so O(n²) in total, which is fine for n ≤ 600. The memory is O(n).
